newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude, gas oil futures retain post-API gains.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude, gas oil futures retain post-API gains.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures on Thursday held onto early gains made on the back of bullish American Petroleum Institute (API) data overnight, traders said.
By 1148 GMT September Brent was 14 cents higher at $18.73 a barrel, with gas oil $1.50 higher at $169.25 a tonne.
"Brent and gas oil are up on the API statistics," one broker said. "But its been pretty quiet other than that."
The API stocks data showed a crude shortfall of 9.7 million barrels, against expectations of a 2.0 million barrel draw, which analysts put down to the effects of Hurricane Danny.
"I think $18.85 a barrel will be resistance for crude," one broker said.
The Brent September/October spread, which has narrowed to around parity from around minus 10 cents two weeks ago, showed demand was picking up in the near-term, traders said.
"We've seen some good buying in the Brent September /October spread,' the broker said. "In the short-term people are quite friendly towards the market."
The API data also showed gasoline stocks fell 3.17 million barrels, up from an expected 1.7 million barrels, brokers said.
Meanwhile traders said the market was waiting for the United Nations to formally approve Iraq's aid distribution plan.
The U.N. was optimistic that its review of Iraq's aid distribution plan could be completed by the end of the week, spokesman Fred Eckhart said on Tuesday.
